open_issues: RecoveryService.cs finding's 'ideally also' suggestion (clear _lastCountedCode when LoginService.OpenSessionAsync resets the profile counters) was left undone: it is explicitly optional in the review text, RecoveryService's _lastCountedCode is private with no clean seam for LoginService to reach, and the mandatory half of the fix (clear on RecoverAsync's own success path) is done and tested via the existing recovery walkthrough tests.
notes:
Applied all findings from the three archived reviews, exactly as prescribed.

verify2-firstrun.json (B1): (1) W07RecoveryDialog.razor now renders the RecoveredNotSignedIn warning card under the new-sheet branch too (previously only shown when no sheet was issued). (2) ConfirmLabel/ConfirmIcon/ConfirmAsync are now gated on `_recoveredWithoutSession` (not just `_newSheet is null`), so a second press of the confirm button closes the dialog instead of re-submitting a recovery that already happened. (3) ActivationService.RollBack now deletes vault blobs written before a mid-activation failure: StoreAttachmentsAsync/StoreAsync collect each VaultStore.Write hash into a `writtenVaultHashes` list scoped to ActivateAsync, and RollBack sweeps them via a new `VaultStore.Delete` (swallows IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException like the existing deletes). Added a walkthrough test (`An_activation_that_fails_after_the_first_attachment_removes_that_attachment_too`) that blocks the guide's vault path with a directory, lets the logo write succeed, then asserts the logo blob is gone after rollback and a clean retry succeeds. (4) RecoveryService.RecoverAsync clears `_lastCountedCode = null` on the Success path. (5) W05Login.razor now runs a `TimeProvider.CreateTimer` (LockService.TickInterval = 15s cadence) while locked out, clearing `_result` and calling StateHasChanged once `Login.LockedUntil()` is null even if the person never types; disposed via `@implements IDisposable`.

verify3-design-verify.json (B1): WInput.razor now stashes the raw keystroke text (`_pendingRaw`) alongside the pending caret/value pair and passes it as a fourth `wakeelUi.setInputValue` argument; app.js's `setInputValue` returns early when `expected !== undefined/null && el.value !== expected`, so a write superseded by a newer keystroke becomes a no-op instead of clobbering it (matches the review's live-reproduced hazard: simultaneous scripted keystrokes with zero delay). WInputTests.cs: the out-of-order test now waits on the terminal `Assert.Equal(new[] { "12" }, values)` instead of the transiently-true invocation count, and both it and a new test (`DateType_PostRenderWrite_CarriesTheProcessedRawTextAsAStaleWriteGuard`) assert the raw-text argument the interop call now carries — bUnit's JSInterop mock doesn't execute real JS, so the actual DOM-level skip is a live/CDP-only behaviour (as the original review verified it too), and that is documented in the test comments.

verify-e2e.json (B0.5), scoped to tests/Wakeel.E2E and the App.xaml.cs comment: GalleryAndAttentionCenterTests.cs's percentage assertion no longer compares the just-written file back to itself; it now asserts `Assert.InRange(percentage, 33.30 ± 0.5)` against a documented baseline (this package's own two verification runs measured 33.3045%), plus a parseable-number check on the artifact file, with a comment telling later B1-B8 packages to express any real threshold the same tolerance-based way. The CDP session is now `DetachAsync()`'d in the same finally block as `Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride`. WakeelE2eFixture.WaitForPageAsync now throws a plain `InvalidOperationException` instead of `WakeelAppLaunchException(processWasKilled: false)` (verified this doesn't affect AppLaunchTimeoutTests, which exercises a different throw site in LaunchedWakeelApp.StartAsync). App.xaml.cs got a documentation-only comment on ConfigureRemoteDebugging's unconditional env-var clear, explaining the silent-override tradeoff without changing behaviour.

Verification: full chain green — `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop` (0/0) → Wakeel.UI.Tests 212/212 → Wakeel.Walkthrough.Tests 19/19 → Wakeel.E2E build 0/0 → Wakeel.E2E tests 4/4, run twice back to back (both times W08 diff 33.3045%, well inside tolerance), zero leaked Wakeel.Desktop.exe after both runs. Final manual host check: Wakeel.Desktop.exe launched on an empty temp --data-folder (port 9345, --window-size=1366x768), /json/list reported /first-run, CDP screenshot (captured via a small PowerShell ClientWebSocket script since the Playwright MCP server was unavailable and the Browser-pane tool talks HTTP not CDP) confirms W02 renders correctly in dark theme — ملف الإعداد, the drop zone, the package-password field with its reveal eye, فحص الحزمة, أين أجد الملف؟, the three-step indicator, footer v0.21 — 16/09/2026 17:40. Host log held exactly one line ("Wakeel desktop host starting up"), no errors, no secrets. Process killed; 0 remaining. One caveat worth noting for the RollBack test: it triggers the failure via `File.Move` onto a pre-existing directory at the guide's vault path, which raises a plain IOException that does not match DiskSpace.IsFull's specific HResult codes, so it exercises the general `catch { RollBack(...); throw; }` path rather than the DiskFull-specific one — both call RollBack identically, so this is a faithful (if indirect) repro of the finding.
